newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chile complains to WTO on US probe into salmon.
newsitem.headline: Chile complains to WTO on US probe into salmon.

text.p: Chile has started a case in the World Trade Organisation (WTO) against a U.S. investigation into its salmon subsidies, trade diplomats said on Wednesday.
Chile requested bilateral consultations be held next month with U.S. officials under the WTO's dispute settlement system -- the first step towards the creation of a neutral panel.
A WTO spokesman confirmed that Chile had requested talks.

Under WTO rules, Washington has 10 days to reply to the request for talks during the first two weeks of September, and must begin talks within 30 days. If no settlement has been reached after 60 days, Chile can ask for a panel to be created.

In its letter to the WTO dated August 5, Chile said the U.S. Department of Commerce decision to initiate a subsidies investigation into salmon imported from Chile was taken "in the absence of sufficient evidence concerning the subsidies investigated and the injury they cause".
This violated the WTO agreement on subsidies and countervailing measures, according to the one-page letter.
